Probably the best pizza in Vietnam
May 2026 • Solo
I never thought to get such a good pizza in Vietnam!!!
Pizza is well topped, not oily at all and the dough is great. The edge is so fluffy inside and out crispy. Perfect!
Needed some salt, but that's how it's supposed to be. Everyone can re-season to their liking - everything is on the table.

When I came in I was greeted very friendly. Service was friendly and fast. All clean.

Before ordering, waiter showed me a plate to show how big the pizzas are here. So no surprise that it corresponds to a small pizza in Germany...

The only downside is that there is only a very limited selection of toppings for pizza.

For me everything was perfect and I wish I could eat there again!!!

Written May 3, 2026
Josep P
Thank you so much for your fantastic review! It really means a lot to us. We’re so happy to see that our Neapolitan-style pizza is finding its place in the hearts of people visiting our restaurant here in Ha Giang.

From the beginning, our idea was simple: to bring the real taste of Naples to this small corner of northern Vietnam. That’s why we use imported ingredients from Italy, many of them coming directly from the south, just like the ones you would find in Napoli itself.

Being considered the top-rated pizzeria in Ha Giang makes us very proud, but what makes us happiest is seeing people enjoy a proper Neapolitan pizza in such a remote and unexpected place.

Thanks again for supporting us and for taking the time to share your experience!

Cela nous fait vraiment plaisir de savoir que la pizza vous a surpris dans le bon sens, surtout la pâte et les garnitures. Le mélange chorizo, gorgonzola et champignons-bacon est d’ailleurs l’un des favoris de beaucoup de voyageurs qui passent par Ha Giang.

Thanks so much for this amazing review!
It really means a lot to us that you came both before and after the Ha Giang Loop.

Reading that this was the best pizza you had in Southeast Asia honestly makes us very proud, especially here in a small mountain town like Ha Giang.
